Red flags: 2023 conviction of the former director for embezzlement
- On 16 May 2022 the Anti-Corruption Service said it was conducting a pre-trial investigation into officials of the National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan over the suspected embezzlement of 146 million tenge of budget money under a 1.2 billion tenge state procurement contract for the international exhibition "Шествие Золотого человека по музеям мира" (The Golden Man's Procession Through the World's Museums), with searches under way with a court's sanction (Tengrinews, 16 May 2022).
- On 20 June 2023 the Interdistrict Criminal Court of Astana, Judge Baglan Idirisov, found Arystanbek Mukhamediuly, the museum's former director and a former minister of culture and sport, guilty under Article 28 part 3 ("organisation of a crime") and Article 189 part 4 ("misappropriation or embezzlement, that is theft of entrusted property on an especially large scale"), and sentenced him to eight years in prison without confiscation of property, with a lifetime ban on holding state service posts (Zakon.kz, Anastasia Prilepskaya, 20 June 2023).
- The court convicted him of embezzling 221,411,730 tenge in staging the "Шествие Золотого человека" exhibition, with the help of his former deputy Almaz Nurazkhan and two other defendants (Zakon.kz).
- Nurazkhan was sentenced to seven years with a lifetime ban on state service posts, and the two other defendants to seven years each (Zakon.kz).

SOURCES
- https://tengrinews.kz/crime/rukovodstvo-natsmuzeya-podozrevaetsya-v-hischenii-antikor-468701/
- https://www.zakon.kz/pravo/6397474-arystanbeku-mukhamediuly-vynesli-prigovor.html
reason: Zakon.kz (20 June 2023, Anastasia Prilepskaya) reports the verdict read by Judge Idirisov: Article 28 part 3 and Article 189 part 4, eight years, no confiscation, lifetime ban, 221,411,730 tenge. Charges now stated as the court did; the two co-defendants with no stated public role are left unnamed. Tengrinews 2022 investigation confirmed.

ID: gapar-aitiev-kyrgyz-national-museum-of-fine-arts-bishkek

WIDER CONTEXT
- In December 2019, 40 named participants of the first Feminnale of Contemporary Art, from 22 countries, published an open letter to the President of Kyrgyzstan saying the minister of culture "arbitrarily banned several works from the show"; they demanded "that Azamat Zhamankulov be removed from office given his professional inaptitude for this position", asked that Mira Dzhangaracheva be reinstated as the museum's director, and called for a ban on censorship in law (open letter posted on Art Leaks, 9 December 2019).
- In April 2021 the Pervomaisky District Court of Bishkek, Judge Saltanat Esenkulova, dismissed the abuse-of-office case against the former director Yuristanbek Shygaev on the grounds of the statute of limitations, with the prosecution supporting the defence's request. According to the investigation, in December 2013 he had two paintings, Nikolai Sverchkov's "Horse and Dog" and Nikolai Ge's "Portrait of Bakunin", removed for scanning without a written order from the Ministry of Culture, and they were damaged; he paid 672,000 soms in compensation (24.kg, Aida Dzhumashova, 22 April 2021).

SOURCES
- https://art-leaks.org/2019/12/09/open-letter-regarding-censorship-at-the-1st-feminnale-of-contemporary-art-kyrgyzstan/ (advocacy source)
- https://24.kg/english/191175_Theft_damage_of_paintings_Case_against_Yuristanbek_Shygaev_dismissed
reason: Letter text confirmed, 40 signatories counted, quotations word for word; 24.kg confirms judge, grounds and 672,000 soms. Both pre-2021 and the case ended without conviction, so WIDER CONTEXT stands.

WIDER CONTEXT
- "Sun on Closed Windows", an Arabic collection of work by 25 Libyan writers edited by Laila Moghrabi and Khaled Mattawa and published in May 2017, is a joint project of the Arete Foundation for Arts and Culture and Darf Publishers of London; after a literary event in Zawiya on 26 August 2017, the Libyan authorities, in particular the Ministry of Culture, condemned its content as against "public morality" and ordered the confiscation of all copies (English PEN, 4 September 2017).
- The writers and editors received death threats, and an Islamic group that controls Zawiya arrested the event's organiser and released him the following day (English PEN, 4 September 2017).
- The Presidency Council's culture and information authority said permission was never given for the book's publication; the publishers said they were given permission in 2013 (Libya Herald, Michel Cousins, 5 September 2017).
- The connection to the space: English PEN names Mattawa as president of the Arete Foundation and the book as an Arete project; neither source names Arete as a target of the ban.

SOURCES
- https://www.englishpen.org/posts/news/libya-fears-for-safety-of-writers-and-editors-over-literary-collection/
- https://libyaherald.com/2017/09/tripoli-cultural-centre-closed-in-book-row/
reason: English PEN ties the book to Arete as a joint project and states the ministry's confiscation order; the space was not itself the target, so the item stays as 2017 WIDER CONTEXT with the connection stated. The other venue's closure is cut, the organiser left unnamed, the Libya Herald URL corrected.

Red flags: 2025 Mexican competition fine on FEMSA's OXXO
- Mexico's Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones (IFT) concluded that Telcel, OXXO and IMMEX coordinated to block AT&T from selling SIM cards in OXXO stores from 12 January 2021 to 24 January 2024, a refusal to deal in breach of Article 10 of the Federal Economic Competition Law, and fined Telcel 1,782.6 million pesos and OXXO and its subsidiary 19.5 million pesos each (Mobile Time Latinoamérica, Aline Sarmiento, 14 July 2025).
- FEMSA said: "no coincidimos con los fundamentos de dicha resolución, ya que no refleja la realidad de nuestro modelo de negocio" (we do not agree with the grounds of that resolution, as it does not reflect the reality of our business model, translated), and said it would challenge the decision in court (Mobile Time Latinoamérica).
- The connection to the collection: Mobile Time Latinoamérica describes OXXO as owned by FEMSA and IMMEX as a FEMSA group company; CIMAM states that "Colección FEMSA is part of Fomento Económico Mexicano, S.A." and has FEMSA's backing.

Red flags: 2023 Chilean competition settlement over OXXO's purchase of OK Market
- Cadena Comercial Andina, the FEMSA company behind OXXO in Chile, agreed to pay 500 annual tax units (about 380 million Chilean pesos) to the state in a partial settlement with the Fiscalía Nacional Económica, approved by the Tribunal de Defensa de la Libre Competencia, after acknowledging that it "no envió dentro del plazo las cartas de renuncia de algunos contratos" (did not send within the deadline the resignation letters for some contracts, translated), a mitigation measure set for its purchase of the OK Market chain (The Clinic, 1 August 2023).
- A second charge by the Fiscalía, over the delivery of false information, was still pending at that date; the company called the Fiscalía's action "excesiva" (excessive, translated) (The Clinic).
- The connection to the collection: The Clinic names Cadena Comercial Andina as the company of Mexico's FEMSA, of which the collection is part (CIMAM).

SOURCES
- https://mobiletime.la/noticias/14/07/2025/att-oxxo-telcel-monopolio/
- https://www.theclinic.cl/2023/08/01/oxxo-debera-pagar-380-millones-fisco-ok-market/
- https://cimam.org/coleccion-femsa/
reason: Ruling: FEMSA is the collection's owner and only named funder, and both decisions are competition sanctions by a regulator or tribunal on FEMSA companies, which meets the name-to-know rule (a funder's company sanctioned, with event, date and authority). Both kept as separate issues; the link now cites CIMAM ('Colección FEMSA is part of Fomento Económico Mexicano, S.A.'). FEMSA is appealing the Mexican fine.

problems: not about the space: the 2018 dispute concerns the Casablanca Biennale, an event of the same founder; Le360 does not mention Ifitry

ID: fondation-ifitry-essaouira

WIDER CONTEXT
- At the fourth Casablanca International Biennale, which opened to the public on 27 October 2018, Merhyl Levisse and 14 other participating artists signed a letter calling the organisation "chaotique", citing unanswered emails and calls, unpaid per diems, restrictions on producing works and no accommodation before the opening for foreign artists; Levisse protested during the opening with a placard and a minute of silence (Le360, Qods Chabaa, 29 October 2018).
- Mustapha Romli, the founder, acknowledged the dysfunctions and said the official sponsor, Casa Event et animation, had withdrawn about three weeks before the opening; he called the ministry's 200,000 dirham budget "dérisoire" (Le360).
- The connection to the residency: the Biennale's website says Mostapha Romli started the Biennale in 2012 and that it grows out of the IFITRY artists' residency, founded in 2008 near Essaouira. The dispute concerns the Biennale, not the residency.

SOURCES
- https://fr.le360.ma/culture/casablanca-grand-cafouillage-a-la-biennale-dart-contemporain-177479/
- https://www.biennalecasablanca.org/en/presentation
reason: Le360 confirms the letter, the placard protest and Romli's reply, but names only the Biennale; a dispute about the operator's other event that no source ties to the residency stays out. File deleted.
